body: A fuel can is paired with a route slip for a field visit; the return line says “full” though the can is nearly empty.
title: Fuel before the run

body:
Repair note: flush the field sprayer at the wrench mark before returning it. The pump seal had softened and the mechanic wrote that the rinse water stung his hands.

The tank held the same treatment mix as the whole season's spray rounds. I kept the page because the batch number was circled twice.
title: Wrench stop after the sprayer run

body:
Cash receipt: fuel at the marked stop, charged to the late-season crop trial. The driver added that the tank was full before the detour to the plots and nearly dry afterward.

The trial lead never signed it. I used the margin to note the plot numbers the driver listed.
title: Gas charged to the trial plot

body:
Notebook line under “you’ll need it”: reserve another can for the second pasture pass. The first crew came home coughing before any emergency convoy used the road.

My mother put it with the household bills so it would not be thrown away. It was the only part of the week that still had a date.

I do not know which of the two accounts was repeated afterward. The older one is the one I had in my hands that day.
title: Fuel needed for a second pass
